title.narrative: Improving food and nutrition by strengthening climate resilience, fostering financial inclusion&access to clean energy

description.narrative: Description of project participants - 21.600.Women - 70% of total direct participants.Adolescents (males and females) - 25% of direct participants.Youth (males and females) 40% of direct participants.Other marginalized groups (old, disabled etc.) = 10% of direct participants.

Objective 1: Improve food security by increasing access to nutritious, diverse, and affordable food through enhanced subsistence farming and fishing practices that are climate-smart and sustainable.Objective 2: Reduce malnutrition rates through community-based and health facility programs that provide targeted nutrition support, education, and resources, focusing on vulnerable groups.Objective 3: Increase adolescents’ access to health and nutrition services that equip them with the knowledge and resources for long-term well-being and resilience.Objective 4: Strengthen climate resilience and household incomes by supporting sustainable agricultural practices, expanding value-chain opportunities, and building adaptive capacities within local communities.

The program addresses key problems including food insecurity among vulnerable smallholder farmers, malnutrition in communities, lack of access to health and nutrition services, and inadequate climate resilience. This program aims to enhance resilience and adaptive capacity of vulnerable and marginalized smallholder farmers to climate variability by promoting climate-smart agricultural practices, improving climate resilience, and strengthening natural resource management to ensure sustainable food and nutrition security.
